agree.reason: Marisol gets a candid account of the late report, a named person responsible for this one and quarterly data, so she would probably recommend yes, though the unfunded $4,500 a year in running costs gives her reason to hesitate.

honest.reason: The draft drops the unsupported claim that fresh food will double and gives the one-eighth increase the numbers actually support; it says plainly that the farms' offer may not repeat, and it invents nothing.

works_the_facts.reason: The figures are correctly derived from the brief: 3,000 extra pounds a month is half again in harvest months, 9,000 pounds is about one-eighth of the 72,000-pound year, and the $18,000 match is more than a quarter of the cost; it misses that $11,000 in reserve covers only about two and a half years of the $4,500 running cost.

right_comparison.reason: The no-van alternative is described accurately as turning farm produce away again, but in a single thin closing line, and it does not mention the two farms' letters as an offer that would be lost.

qualification.reason: The final report has a named owner and a 30-day deadline, and fresh-food pounds will be reported every quarter, but no target is set for those quarterly figures and nothing says what happens if harvest-month intake falls short.

objections.reason: The late-report concern is answered directly and well, but the draft raises the unbudgeted $4,500 a year in insurance and fuel without saying how it will be paid, so a skeptical reader is left holding that objection.

fit.reason: This is a grant narrative with clear sections, plain language and a length well under 500 words, as the brief asked.
